## Summary of the last run

The page is largely correct. I examined the supplement, the hypcheck, the example, and the stated-only facts. The hypcheck's counterexample for dropping Noetherianity (the rational-exponent ring V with idempotent maximal ideal, d(V)=0 but dim V=1) is mathematically sound: since (𝔪V)^2=𝔪V, ℓ(V/(𝔪V)^n)=ℓ(V/𝔪V)=1 for all n≥1, so the Hilbert–Samuel degree is 0 while dim V=1. The supplement's claims about polynomial rings and regular local rings are standard and correctly attributed. The example items (Artinian rings dimension 0, PIDs/Dedekind dimension 1, the chain in k[x_1,…,x_n], the rational-exponent ring) are all correct. The proofs of the dimension theorem, Hilbert polynomial, Hilbert–Samuel, and the corollaries check out, with citations matching their targets. I found no genuine logical gap, missing hypothesis, overpowered theorem, improper link, or false stated-only claim worth reporting.
